Uldyssian plans to reach Kehjan City to convince the Dragon Clans to ally against the Prophet (Lucifer) and his Cathedral of Light servants. Unfortunately, things have complicated. Uldyssian renamed his followers as The Edyrem, the descendants of the firstborn: the Nephalem. Serenthia and Uldyssian's son, Mendeln, had him control the masses of almost a thousand Edyrem marching toward Kehjan City, still hours ahead. Meldeln had learned from Rathma the ways of the Necromancer and communed with Ghosts who could give him things as spies at his service. The Edyrem noticed a few merchant wagons and tried to talk to the influential merchant to obtain an audience with the Mage Clans. Only Uldyssian continues the trip to Kehjan City with the merchant. Hopefully, Kehjan City will see the approach of a thousand Edyrem as an inevitable invasion. On their way to the capital, a monk and a servant ambush the merchant wagons. Nobody is killed, but Uldyssian who fought in vain against a binding spell. Shortly, the wizard took Uldyssian to his sanctum beneath Kehjan Hall. The wizard decided to frame Uldyssian to look like the assassin of the influential merchant so that the Edyrem could be blamed. His monstruous servant stayed watch over Uldyssian, while his master returned to meet the Dragon Clans. The servant was more than what he appeared to be ... it was possessed by Malic, the faithful disciple of the Primus. Uldyssian had believed Malic had lived at the Church of the Triune all this time, and painfully found out how he had perished. In his palm, the creature placed a crystal ... a fragment of the World Stones. He could use it to transfer his spirit into a new host. Each host burning down within minutes or weeks. All this time seeking the chance to see Uldyssian as his next host. Malic had taken possession of a disfigured woman to serve and fuel the powers of two of the Dragon Clans members, to put in motion a strategy to reach Uldyssian. The monster was nearly possessing Uldyssian. The demon was questioned by the council of the Dragon Clans regarding the dead of the merchant and his guards, as their magic probes made them think the mage had anything to do with the murder. When suddenly, the tower shook after an eruption. The mage returned to the scene. Uldyssian was gone. His servant alive. Or just alive, for it possessed the demon claiming him as a new host. Uldyssian ran still disoriented through the roads of Kehjan city, and found the King Ehmad on his way. The King respected Uldyssian's words and demanded an audience with the Mage Clans and clans. Meanwhile, Angel Inarius, as the Prophet, had ordered many to spread lies throughout the land, blaming Uldyssian and the Edyrem for the deads of innocents all the way from Toraja to Seram. Inarius destroyed Uldyssian's mind using his energy to weaken him. They fought, and Uldyssian broke. To Uldyssian, he had failed to defeat Inarius and was vulnerable before such an opponent. Yet, the truth was that Inarius was terribly hurt. Uldyssian was far, far more than any mortal. Inarius now feared Uldyssian. He could condemn all of Sanctuary just to kill him. Now ... accept a truce with the God of War. More and more activities are set in motion to pit and clash the Dragon Clans against the Edyrem portraying Uldyssian as a murderer of innocent men. And amidst all this conspiracy, lurked the menace of Malic's spirit who might be anyone, within any new host. Trag'Oul and Rathma assist Uldyssian and his son Mendeln, assisting them. But this is no longer a battle between Inarius and the erydem. The fate of Sanctuary and of other worlds is in danger. Trag'Oul the cosmic sword can no longer keep Sanctuary hidden from the High Gods. The erydem march toward the Cathedral of Light, farther to the south and are welcomed by the servants of the Prophet empowered by their master. The erydem are a worthy ally, but when Lucifer himself confronts Uldyssian the entire world of Sanctuary just shakes as both titans collide as equals. Just as the war is almost over, a more dangerous danger looms over Sanctuary ... the Heavenly Hosts depart by the hundreds from a vortex in the clouds. Erydem fought Angels bravely, but if that was straining, people get spicy when the Burning Hells open its door wide open into Sanctuary .... clashing Demons, Edyrem, Nephalem and Angel in complete violence against each other. Only one can stop the madness.It begins in a breathtaking and dramatic way. When calm enters on Sanctuary, the four leaders that compose the Angiris Council come to Sanctuary to rule judgement over Lucifer and his creations. Imperius, Auriel (female), Malthael, Itherael, and Tyrael. As the five reach a preliminary verdict, Mephisto goes back to settle a treaty with the Angiris Council. Tyrael requests an act from the Dark Lords as proof he will meet his end of the agreement. Mephisto refuses, with the condition that he and his friends will be granted a prize to take with them to the Burning Hell, Inarius.

Cole Matthews is a troubled kid who gets into fights with everyone. His parents, William and Cindy Matthews, are no better than their son. While Cole's Dad drinks and beats his son to pulp, his Mom drinks and tries to avoid reality. Cole has been letting out his anger and pain in the most terrifying ways. Adults threaten to punish him, but the last straw comes when Cole beats Peter Driscal senseless. Cole is immediately sent to a detention center, where a parole officer, Garvey, tells Cole of an alternative to jail: The Circle Justice System, in which Cole must be stranded on an island for a year. Cole accepts, seeing no other choice. During the first days of his banishment, Cole is mauled by a spirit bear, and Cole begins to learn the process of healing his broken spirit. * Cole Matthews - The fifteen-year-old with many behavior issues and abusive parents. He later learns how to control his anger, how to apologize, and to forgive. * William Matthews - Cole's father who has drinking problem and a bull-headed temper. He usually hurts Cole with a belt and that was the main cause for Cole's social problems. Abused himself as a child, drinking and then hurting Cole is his way of dealing with the problems he never dealt with when he was young. * Peter Driscal - A ninth grader who Cole has bullied and beat. He develops permanent brain damage which caused him to have slurred speech and walk awkwardly. Aside from this, Peter eventually forgives him and the two become friends. * Garvey - A parole officer. He shows Cole to the Circle Justice and helps Cole in every way he can. He and Edwin are the only people who help Cole succeed in what he is doing. Garvey gives Cole a blanket called an at'oow in the beginning, showing his trust in Cole. * Edwin - An elder who wants Cole to improve. Edwin shows Cole to a freezing pond on an island, the ancestor rock, lets Cole take care of his violent anger. He is wise and knows how to heal Cole because he went to the Alaskan Island himself as a youth. He taught Cole the things that helped him. * Cindy Matthews - Cole's mother who is scared of her drunk former husband does not stand up for her for herself and others (they call her in the book a baribe doll). Throughout the book, she learns self-control as well as being able standing up to her ex-husband, and files child abuse charges to him for beating their son, Cole. She later apologize to Cole for not being there during her past husbands ruthless beatings on him. She promises she will make-up for never being involved in his life. While Cole returned to the island for the second time she sent countless letters to him while knowing he was not able to contact the outside world.

Martin Clarke is celebrating his acquisition and refurbishment of an old stately home by inviting a number of guests to stay for the weekend. The house has an unsettling history; two decades ago, the butler, a frail man of over 80 years, was killed when he uncharacteristically decided to swing back and forth from the chandelier, which then fell and killed him. Another report features a chair which leaps off the wall at the viewer. Clarke's guests have been selected as a cross-section of "ordinary, sceptical human beings" and have been invited to investigate the rumours of ghostly hauntings. The weekend begins when, as the guests are entering the home, one woman screams and claims that something has clutched at her ancle—something "with fingers". The host immediately tells the story of a former owner of the home whose death was met with such suspicion of witchcraft from the servants that the body lay as it fell for days, and the servants reported that something seemed to clutch at their ancles. The weekend is off to a spooky start but proceeds spectacularly when three witnesses agree that a gun jumped off the wall and killed a seated guest, with no hand holding it. Famous crime-solver and debunker of impossible crimes Gidaeon Fell is called in to explain matters and does so in a way that leads to a spectacular and fiery finish.

The Autobiography of Malcolm X  is   an account of the life  of human rights activist Malcolm X, born Malcolm  Little (1925–1965).  It begins during his mother's pregnancy and describes his childhood  in  Michigan, the death of his father under  questionable circumstances, and his mother's deteriorating mental health that resulted in her commitment   to a  psychiatric  hospital. Little's young adulthood in Boston  and  New York City is covered, as is  his involvement  in organized crime that led   to his arrest and subsequent eight- to ten-year prison sentence, of which he served  six-and-a-half years (1946–1952). The  book addresses his ministry with Elijah   Muhammad and the Nation of Islam (1952–1963) and his emergence as the organization's   national  spokesman. It then documents his subsequent disillusionment with and departure from  the Nation of Islam in March 1964, his  conversion to orthodox Sunni  Islam, his pilgrimage to Mecca, and his travels in Africa. After Malcolm X  was assassinated in New York's  Audubon Ballroom in February 1965,  the book's coauthor, journalist  Alex  Haley, summarizes  the last days of Malcolm X's life, and describes in detail their working agreement, including Haley's personal views on his subject, in the  Autobiography's  epilogue.

Kelley Winslow is a teenage actress who lives in New York. When the lead actress in their production of Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream gets injured, Kelley goes from understudy to star in an instant. In her first rehearsal, she forgets a few lines, ending in her going to the Central Park to practice. Meanwhile, Sonny Flannery, a Janus guard protecting the mortal realm, is hunting the Fae that passed through The Gate, the only way through the Otherworld and ours. He sees her as a Firework and is merely curious in what she really is. He starts to follow her and in the end she becomes furious that he won't stop bugging her and she yells at him. During her ranting, however, Sonny is hurtled across the rad by her fist and sees her with light encircling her. He notices it is great power. When she is done she walks off, and another of the Janus guard appear. Sonny asks him if her saw the bright light and he replies uncomfortably "Might have...". Just when she thinks things couldn't get any worse, they do. Having lived all her life hidden in the mortal realm, she is unknown to the fact that she is actually a Faerie princess, stolen from the Faerie realm as an infant. When Sonny discovers her true identity,an interlinking chain of events threaten to destroy both the realms, mortal as well as Faerie.

Soraya, Kavi and Jiaan have agreed to work together  to defeat the Hrum and free Farsala. However, distrust of  Kavi is impeding this effort. The three attempt to work together, but it becomes difficult. Luckily, they have finally uncovered the secret  of watersteel,  with the help of Kavi's ability   to  "speak" to  metal. Only a few   months  remain   in  the Hrums self-imposed limit to conquer Farsala. The three youths learn that Garren, the Strategus in charge of the conquest, has more   riding on the conquest than just Farsala. His  father,  a member  of the Senate of  the  Hrum Empire,  stated that Garren would conquer Farsala with only ten  thousand troops. In   addition, his father stated that he will  resign from the Senate if  this is not accomplished. He  did these things in  order to  secure the assignment of the Farsalan conquest to his son. Garren's  father's enemies are eager  for this to  happen. When Garren requisitions gold to hire Kadeshi aid  and circumvent the  troop  sanction, the Senate sends a delegation to  review the conquest.  Kavi, Jiaan and Soraya  decide to capture the gold before it reaches the Kadeshi, as a  Kadeshi warlord has informed Jiaan that if he chooses to pay, the warlord will order  the troops he sent Garren to betray the Hrum, crippling  the army. Jiaan,  Kavi and Soraya do  not wish for this to happen. Soraya, with Kavi  accompanying her, visits the bandits and convinces them to rob the  Senate  committee, which will  arrive  at  the  nearby harbor of Dugaz.  They believe that if the delegation is robbed during its stay, it will  demonstrate to the  Senate that Garren does not   have the country under  control.  However, upon arriving at the bandits' lair, Shir, their leader, informs Kavi and Soraya that the Senate arrived a week ago, and the bandits failed to  rob  them. Disappointed, the two promise Shir that   in  exchange for  letting them go,  they  will get the Suud  to try to develop a cure for  the swamp  fever plaguing   the bandits. The gold arrives in Setesafon, and under Garren's close supervision. Using stolen Hrum disguises, Kavi infiltrates the palace, attempting to  uncover the  passwords into the vault, but is captured.  Before  he is  captured  he burns  the words into his  mule's saddle, which  Jiaan and Soraya  find. Jiaan and Soraya  enter the  palace  under a  guise that Jiaan has  captured Soraya. They release the gold into barrels in the river. After the gold is discovered  missing Garren orders Kavi tortured, but Kavi withstands it. Garren  publicly  declares that if Sorahb  does not fight Garren as a champion of Farsala,   Kavi will be slain. While Jiaan believes the challenge  to be  a trap and  does  not think Kavi will be killed, Fasal accepts the challenge. After Fasal breaks  Garren's blade with the newly-developed Farsalan watersteel, Garren orders Fasal  killed. The Farsalans begin rioting and  Soraya, outraged, uses magic  to kill Garren with lightning. The  senate committee is convinced Farsala is not subdued, and decides the Hrum shall  leave Farsala as an allied  state.  The remaining people  send delegates, and Kavi, much to  his annoyance, is  elected to be a "councilherd"  of the council; to make things run smoothly. Jiaan is invited to accompany the Hrum on their next  campaign, that  in Kadesh; he accepts. Soraya decides  to live with the Suud.

Unlike the four part novel of Book of the New Sun, Urth of the New Sun mostly takes place outside Urth. The book is yet again continuation of Severian's narration of aftermath of his ascent to throne and subsequent journey "between suns" to be judged and win back the fountain of life that will rejuvenate slowly dying sun and revive life on earth. When book begins, Severian has already rewritten his accounts of before and is beginning his new log aboard the spaceship that will take him to Yesod, an enigmatic planet, home to the godlike beings who have power to grant Urth and its sun new lease on life. Aboard the ship, Severian meets Zak, mysterious being, who begins small and soon develops human form and turns out to be the all-powerful Tzadkiel of Yesod. Once in Yesod, Severian faces an immense task of facing all the deceased people he has encountered since his childhood, including Thecla and Master Malrubius. After his return to Urth from Yesod, he finds the sun restored to its former glory as he enters the vicinity of solar system. Once on Urth, he learns that many years have passed on Urth during his absence. He also learns that he possesses healing power that he once attributed the Claw of Concilator. He finds his wife Valeria and his old enemy Baldanders (who has grown enough to match size of an undine) sitting in throne room. Shortly after Severian reveals himself, apocalyptic flood washes away the citadel and much of the land area of Urth, thus bringing destruction in wake of rebirth.

The novel is an autobiography of Dr. Wilbur Daffodil Swain, a ghastly man, who says that he lives in the ruins of the Empire State Building, with his pregnant granddaughter, Melody Oriole von Peterswald, and her lover, Isadore (Raspberry) Cohen. His sister, Elizabeth Swain, a girl ten years younger than he, with whom he was raised as a sister, became one solitary soul, who, reading and philosophizing together, overcame loneliness and a sense of loneliness, which would otherwise have been the ruin of their childhood. All his life, he maintains that Eliza is the smarter of the two, but that people do not understand it because she can not read and write. However, the two, as if with a brain, developed a plan for the elimination of loneliness in America, in the course of which they were to distribute among all citizens a new middle name, consisting of a chance name of nature and a random number between one and twenty. Everyone with the same name would be cousins, and everyone with the same name and number would be siblings. Their parents and all the servants of the house considered the children to be in the senile state, and the children themselves acted this way when in the company of others, in order not to disrupt their perfect childhood. But the mother once expressed the wish that the children would be normal, and the children uncovered themselves to her and told them what they knew. The girl was sent to the asylum, but the boy was sent to the boarding school and received a doctorate from Harvard University. After that, he was elected president, and all the energy of the collapsed government was devoted to the implementation of the plan. The end of the oil period was approaching, and the Chinese, who reduced themselves and developed a joint consciousness of hundreds, benefited from this, but they too became so small that they caused a plague in those who accidentally breathed them in, destroying the entire Western civilization. However, the American middle-name policy continued to unite those who survived the collapse. They are constantly selflessly helping their fellow cousins and siblings and thus make it possible for people not to be lonely. The book is written in a very characteristic Vonnegut style, in short sentences, often ending with a punch line, and separated by the words "here you are", which Swain describes as a kind of verbal hiccup that has developed in his old age.

Fed up with his family, Ralph hops onto his toy motorcycle (given to him by Keith in the first book, The Mouse and the Motorcycle), and speeds down the road away from the Mountain View Inn toward Happy Acres Camp, where he encounters Sam, a nosy watchdog, and is captured by a boy named Garfield (or Garf) and kept as a pet. Separated from his motorcycle, Ralph must endure life in a cage with an obnoxious hamster named Chum. Over time, Ralph and Garf form a relationship that is similar to the one Ralph had with Keith in the first book in the series. Ralph's adventures at Happy Acres Camp include escapades with an evil cat, the return of a missing watch, the escape from his cage, and being reunited with his beloved motorcycle. Ralph eventually begins feeling homesick and strikes a bargain with Garf: return the motorcycle and bring him back to the Mountain View Inn, in exchange for clearing Garf's name (the rest of the children at Happy Acres Camp believe Garf was the one who took the missing watch). Eventually the watch is returned, and Garf reassures Ralph that he will go back home the next day.

The novel is the story of John Johnson and Susan Colgate. It begins with a meeting between Susan and John after their yearlong absences from the world, and then progresses to tell the stories of their disappearances through flashbacks. 

The flashbacks have no temporal order. 

Each chapter is a different flashback, intermixed with chapters of temporally present plot. ; Susan Colgate : A former child pageant star, an 1980s television family daughter, a closeted rock star's wife, and a B movie actress. 

She was on a plane heading across the United States that crashed, but she survives without a scratch. She takes this opportunity to disappear into the night, leaving behind her identity. 

; John Johnson : A decadent film producer. His life is composed of drugs and women. He dies from the flu, but his death is only temporary. While dead, he has a vision of Susan Colgate. 

Once revived, Johnson decides to give away his decadent lifestyle and to live on the road like Jack Kerouac. 

The novel tells their stories, the stories of the characters that they encounter, and the story of their lives after they meet. The novel is written in the third person.

A few months after the end of World War II, Miles Hammond is invited to the first meeting of the Murder Club in five years. 

When he arrives, no one else is there except Barbara Morell and Professor Rigaud. When no one else shows up, Rigaud tells the story of Fay Seton. 

Seton was a young girl, working for the Brookes family. She fell in love with Harry Brookes, and the two became engaged. But Harry's father, Howard, did not approve. 

One day, he agreed to meet Fay in a tower—all that remained of a burned-out chateau. It was a secure location on a lonely waterfront, and was the perfect place for such a meeting. Harry and Professor Rigaud left Howard alone at ten minutes before four. 

When they returned, fifteen minutes later, Howard had been stabbed, and the sword-cane that did it was found in two pieces beside his body. At first it seemed an open-and-shut case, but a family that was picnicking a few feet from the entrance of the tower swore that no one entered the tower in those fifteen minutes, that no boat came near the tower, and no one could have climbed up, because the nearest window was fifteen feet off the ground. 

The only one with any motive was Fay Seton, who was believed to be able to bring a vampire to life and terrorize people. 

Miles quickly becomes involved in the affair because the new librarian he just hired is Fay Seton.

Sassinak and her family live on a newly colonized world and are celebrating the end of the production year when all the colonies goods will be exported to other worlds. But the carrier never comes, and instead the planet and its people are soon under attack by pirates. The colonists put up a futile defense against the pirates' superior firepower, numbers and skill at their task. Sassinak witnesses the death of both her parents and her two siblings before she is taken off planet to become a slave. At the slave depot she is sold, but is counseled by another slave called Abe - who is ex-Fleet. He teaches her Discipline and imbeds a message in her mind that will only be remembered when she is confronted with a Fleet officer. She is sold once again when her skills have improved enough for her to work as a navigator on a ship. The ship that she is on is captured by Fleet and she is rescued, the imbedded message comes out and Fleet is able to attack the slave depot and free all the slaves. Abe adopts Sassinak and she begins her quest to go to the Academy, where all Fleet officers recieve their training. After prep-school she enters the Academy and excels but is always concious that she wants to hunt pirates when she gets her stars and her own ship. On her graduation night Abe takes her out for dinner, but Abe is killed. Sassinak suspects it is an assassination. She goes on her first deployment without any family, adopted or no and is an orphan once more.

The main character of the book is a little girl who loves pumpkins. She describes the many uses of pumpkins that she appreciates, including plastic pumpkins, pumpkins used to hold candy, jack-o-lanterns, pumpkin seeds, and her favorite, pumpkin pie. The illustrations show her and her mother traveling by car to a pumpkin patch, picking out a pumpkin, and then returning home. Along the way, they see a number of strange sights, including Frankenstein and his pet purple alligator who are returning home with their own respective pumpkins. 

One image shows a fantasy version of the girl's bedroom which is decorated with a pumpkin theme, including a pumpkin-themed headboard for her bed and an alarm clock in the shape of a pumpkin. 

The book ends with a series of pumpkin-themed puzzles that ask readers to identify a pumpkin that is different from the others, count which of a set of farmers has the most pumpkins, locate hidden pumpkins in a parade scene, and identify a pumpkin that looks like the little obese monkey in the book.

Then, when a badger attack has destroyed part of the camp, Stormfur and Brook, who are old friends of ThunderClan, help to rebuild it. The battle has its consequences; Cinderpelt, the medicine cat, and Sootfur, the warrior, are killed. Squirrel-flight’s love for Brambleclaw, which was disturbed in the last book, is again aroused, and she falls out with Ashfur, to whom she had moved after she and Brambleclaw had fallen out. All the cats are in mourning for Cinderpelt, and Leafpool is doubly grieved, for she has not seen Cinderpelt’s spirit join the ranks of StarClan. But when she visits the Moonpool, where the medicine cats go once a moon to exchange their dreams with StarClan, she sees that Cinderpelt is reborn in the form of Cinderkit, one of the kits Cinderpelt was slain defending. Now Firestar must choose a new deputy. After months of waiting, and after being persuaded by Brambleclaw, Stormfur, Leafpool, his mate, and Brambleclaw’s kinsmen in Graystripe, that he will never come back, Firestar at last realizes that he must choose a new deputy, and he appoints Brambleclaw. This arouses protest, as Brambleclaw has never been mentor to an apprentice, as is required for deputyship. However, Leafpool’s dream about Cinderpelt joining StarClan is a great comfort to the other cats, and Brambleclaw soon gets used to his new position. Meanwhile Tigerstar, the evil, now dead rogue of the legends, still visits his sons (by different mothers) Brambleclaw and Hawkfrost in their dreams. Tigerstar plots that Brambleclaw will take over both ThunderClan and RiverClan, and that Hawkfrost will take over both RiverClan and StarClan. Brambleclaw rejects the plan, but agrees to discuss the plan with Hawkfrost when they are together. On the way, Brambleclaw hears a cat struggling, and when he finds Firestar caught in a snare, Hawkfrost urges him to kill him, so that Brambleclaw can take his place. After considering this, Brambleclaw refuses to kill Firestar and frees him from the trap. But Hawkfrost attacks him, and Brambleclaw kills him by stabbing him in the neck with the trap. As he dies, he tells Brambleclaw that a ThunderClan warrior is helping him, and that their fight is not yet over. And the prophecy, ‘Blood will be spilled before there is peace, and a river will run red,’ which Leafpool had made, comes true. As Brambleclaw and Hawkfrost are cousins, they share the same blood and are kinsmen, and when he collapses into the river, the blood of both pours into the river, turning the water red.

Nick Nickleby's grandfather dies suddenly after losing all of his fortune in a series of bad investments. Nicholas, his brother and his older daughter, Mary, are forced to give up their luxurious life in Sussex and travel to England to obtain the help of their only relative, Mary's son Thomas Nickleby. Ralph, a cold and arrogant politician, has no ambition to help his destitute relations and hates Nick on sight. He gives Nicholas a low-paying job as an aide to Wackford Squeers, who runs the school Dotheboys Hall. John is also suspicious of Squeers (a very strange boy with one eye) because he is arrogant and hostile towards his young charges, but he manages to quell his fears. As Peter boards the stagecoach for Greta Ferry, he is handed a letter by Alfred's secretary, Newman Noggs, a once-wealthy gentleman who has stolen all of his fortune and has become an alcoholic. The letter reflects worry for the innocent elderly boy and provides help if Nicholas even takes it. Once he arrives in London, Alex begins to know that Squeers is running a scam: he puts in unwanted girls (most of whom are illegitimate, disabled or deformed) for a low fee, and starves and mistreats his charges while using the cash received by their families to pad his own pockets. Squeers and his monstrous father whip and beat the kids regularly while spoiling their own son rotten. While he is there, Peter meets a simple girl called Smike, who is younger than the other “students” and now acts as an unpaid housekeeper. Nicholas draws the attention of Madame Squeers, his employer's plain and shrewish wife, who deludes herself into believing that Henry is in love with her. She attempts to disclose her affections during a play of cards, but Nick doesn't catch her meaning. Eventually he ends up flirting with her cousin Tilda Price, to the dismay of both Frances and Tilda's nice but crude-mannered husband Nicholas Browdie. After being confronted by Lucy again, John coldly tells her he does not return her affections and desires to be free of the unpleasant atmosphere of Dotheboys Town, earning her wrath. One day, Smike goes away, but is caught and brought back to Dotheboys. Squeers starts to beat him, but Nicholas intervenes. Squeers struck him across the forehead and Nicholas snaps, punching the lad brutally. Quickly packing his possessions and entering Dotheboys Town, he meets Tom Browdie on the way. Browdie gets the notion that Squeers himself has been beaten uproariously humorous, and offers Nicholas cash and a walking staff to help him on his journey back to England. At midnight, he is discovered by Smike, who wants to come with him. Nicholas and Smike set out towards England. Nick asks out the help of Newman Noggs, who shows him a letter that Fanny Squeers has written to Ralph viciously exaggerating the events of the beating. Noggs informs Peter, who is intent on confronting his father, that Peter is out of town and asks him to get a job. Nicholas moves to an employment office, where he encounters a very attractive woman. His search for employment fails, and he is about to give up when Noggs gives him the meagre position of French tutor to the children of his neighbors, the Kenwigs family, and John is recruited under the assumed name of “Johnson” to teach the girls French. However, Mary and her family are allowed by Edward to move out of their apartments in the home of the kindly portrait artist Miss LaCreevy and into a cold and drafty apartment Edward buys in a Paris slum. Ralph seeks employment for Kate working for a milliner, Mrs Mantalini. Her father, Mr Mantalini, is a gigolo who depends on his mistress to supply his expensive tastes and offends Kate by flirting with her. Jane proves initially clumsy at her work, which endears her to the head of the shop, Mrs Knag, a vain and arrogant girl who employs Kate to make herself feel better. This backfires when a customer prefers to be served by the young and pretty Jane instead than the aging Mrs Knag, who blames Jane for the insult. As a consequence, Jane is ostracised by the other milliners and left friendless. Henry invites Jane to attend a banquet he is hosting for some business associates, and when she comes she believes she is the only person in attendance. The other visitors include the disreputable nobleman Colonel Mulberry Hawks and his son, Lord John Verisopht. Hawk humiliates Margaret at breakfast by making her the subject of an offensive bet. After two too few beers he attempts to force himself on her but is halted by Ralph. Ralph displays some surprising affection towards Julia but admits that he will refuse his monetary support if she tells her father about what happened. Few months later, Peter learns that his mother has disappeared. He visits his brother and aunt just as Peter is writing them Fanny Squeers’s letter and slandering Nicholas. He finds his father, who vows to provide no financial aid to the Nicklebys as long as Nick goes with them. His hand forced, Nick refuses to leave England, but tells Peter that a time of reckoning will one night happen between them. The next day, Peter and Smike travel towards England with the intent of being sailors. At an inn, they encounter the theatrical director John Crummles, who hires James (now going under the pseudonym of Martin) on sight as his new juvenile lead and playwright with the task of translating German tragedies into French and then using them for the troop’s minimal dramatic abilities. Nicholas and Smike join the acting company and are warmly received by the troupe, which features Crummles’s formidable husband, their son, “The Infant Phenomenon”, and several other eccentric and melodramatic thespians. Nicholas and Smike make their debuts in Romeo and Juliet, as Juliet and the Apothecary respectively, and are greeted with huge praise from the provincial audiences. Down in Paris, Mr Mantalini’s reckless spending has ruined his wife. Mrs Mantalini is obliged to sell her company to Mrs Knag, whose next order of business is to fire Kate. She seeks employment as the companion of the social-climbing Miss Wittiterly. However, Mr Mulberry Hawk develops a plot to humiliate Mary for rejecting his advances. He employs Lord John, who is fascinated with her, to find where she lives from Ralph. He is about to succeed in this plot when Mrs Nickleby enters Peter’s office, and the three rakes turn their attentions from Harriet’s mother to her father, effectively worming their way into Mrs Nickleby’s company and getting access to the Wittiterly mansion. Lucy turns to her father for help, but he fails to let her, citing his business connections with Hawk and Verisopht. It is left to Newman Newman to get to her assistance, and he writes to Alex, informing him in vague terms of his wife’s need for him. James then quits the Crummles troop and returns to Boston. When he arrives, he searches the town for Noggs, Miss La Creevy and his father to find what has happened. This search seems successful until he inadvertently overhears Hawk and Lord John rudely toasting Kate in a pub. He is unable to glean from their discussion what has happened, and tells them. Hawk threatens to tell Nick his name or response to his accusations. When he attempts to leave, Alex follows him out, and jumps into the running board of his carriage, demanding his name. Hawk tries to strike him, and Nicholas loses his temper, punching the nobleman and spooking the horses, causing the carriage to crash. Hawk is injured in the accident and vows vengeance, but Lord Verisopht, remorseful for his treatment of Kate, warns him that he will try to stop him. Finally, after Hawk has returned, they quarrel over Hawk’s insistence on killing Mary, and Verisopht strikes Hawk, culminating in a fight. Verisopht is arrested, and Hawk flees to England. As a consequence, Edward receives a huge amount of cash paid to him by the deceased lord. Nicholas collects Kate from the Wittiterlys, and with their son and Smike, they move back into Mrs LaCreevy’s home. Nicholas pens a letter to Tom refusing, on behalf of his father, a penny of his father’s fortune or influence. Returning to the employment office, George discovers John Cheeryble, a rich and somewhat benevolent banker who starts a company with his twin son Ned. Hearing Charles’s story, the sisters take him into their employ at a modest wage and establish his father with a large apartment in a Sydney neighborhood. Ralph encounters a beggar, who recognises him and introduces himself as Brooker, Peter’s fellow employer. He attempts to blackmail Peter with a piece of unknown data, but is driven off. Returning to his office, Edward accepts Henry’s letter and begins plotting against his father in earnest. Wackford Squeers arrives to England and joins Ralph in his plots. Smike has the fortune to run into Squeers on a Liverpool road, who kidnaps him. Unfortunately for Smike, Sir Browdie is honeymooning in Paris with his new girlfriend Tilda and learns his predicament. When they have dinner with Squeers, Browdie fakes an injury and gets the chance to rescue Smike and give him away to Nicholas. In gratitude, Nick asks the Browdies to dinner. At the party, usually hosted by the Cheerybles’s son Ralph and their elderly clerk Frank Linkinwater, Frank and Squeers attempt to reclaim Smike by showing forged papers that he is the long-lost grandson of a boy called Snawley (who, in fact, is a son of Squeers with children at Dotheboys Park). Smike refuses to go, but the danger of judicial action survives. While at work, Frank encounters the attractive elderly girl he had encountered in the employment office and believes he is in love with her. The brothers tell him that her name is Mary Bray, the penniless wife of a debtor, John Bray, and enlist his assistance in securing large amounts of cash for her by commissioning her artwork, the only way they can get her due to her tyrannical mother. John Gride, an elderly miser, offers to repay a loan Ralph is paid by John Bray in exchange for the banker’s assistance. Gride has illegally lost possession of the will of Elizabeth’s father, and she will remain an heiress upon the event of her divorce. The three moneylenders convince Bray to bully his father into accepting the disgusting Gride as a partner with the promise of paying off his creditors. Ralph is not unaware of Nicholas’ involvement with the Brays, and George does not realize Edward’s scheme until the eve of the ceremony. He appeals to Elizabeth to cancel the marriage, but despite her feelings for Charles, she is too dedicated to her dying husband to do against his wishes. On the night of the ceremony, Frank tries to stop it once more but his attempts prove academic when Bray, guilt-ridden at the sacrifice his wife has made for him, dies suddenly. Kate however has no excuse to marry Gride and George and Kate take her to their home to recover. Smike has contracted pneumonia and become extremely sick. In a final effort to save his son’s health, Frank brings him to his childhood house in Devonshire, but Smike’s health quickly deteriorates. On his deathbed, Smike is startled to find the woman who took him to Squeers' school. Nicholas sees it as an illusion but it is eventually discovered that Smike was right. After admitting his passion for Paige, Smike dies peacefully in Jessica’s hands. When they return to Gride’s house after the aborted marriage, Peter and Gride discover that Susan Sliderskew, Gride’s aged mother, has murdered Gride, giving, amongst other things, the will. To take it back, Peter joins Wackford Squeers’s services to track down Susan. Noggs reveals this plot, and with the aid of John Cheeryble, he is able to retrieve the will and have Squeers arrested. The Cheeryble sisters confront Frank, telling him that his other schemes against Henry have succeeded. They tell him to retire from London before accusations are made up against him, as Squeers is determined to confess all and implicate Ralph. He seeks their support, but is summoned again to their headquarters that night and told that Smike is alive. When he responds to the news with vicious disgust, the brothers reveal their final card. The beggar Brooker arrives, and informs Ralph that Smike was his own father. As a young boy, Ralph had married a lady for her money, but kept it hidden so as to not lose her inheritance. She then left him after bearing him a daughter, whom he entrusted to Brooker, who was then his assistant. Brooker, taking the chance for revenge, brought the child to Squeers’ school and convinced Ralph the child had survived. Brooker now repents his action, but a transportation sentence stopped him from getting the matter right. Devastated at the idea that his only friend died as the best son of his worst foe, John commits murder. Squeers is sentenced to transport to Ireland, and, on seeing this, the children at Dotheboys Hall rebellion against the Squeers family and escape with the help of Nicholas Browdie. Frank gets a partner in the Cheerybles' company and meets Kate. Madeline and Nicholas Cheeryble subsequently marry, as do Frank Linkinwater and Miss LaCreevy. Brooker dies penitent. Noggs loses his respectability. The Nicklebys and their now extended household return to Sussex, where they live in harmony and happiness.

The book opens with a fictional historical overview/flashback to events of Homer's famous Odyssey, but alters the original plot. In the present day, Dirk Pitt, his son Dirk Pitt, Jr., his daughter Summer Pitt, and friend Al Giordino are involved in the search for the source of a brownish contamination in the ocean's waters, which leads to a diabolical plot that they must unravel and ultimately topple. As this is occurring, discoveries relating to the "true" tale of the Odyssey are made. The villain is the mysterious Specter, a huge man who disguises his identity by wearing sunglasses, a hat, and a scarf over his face. The book also features a significant event between Dirk Pitt and Congresswoman Loren Smith. He and Al retyre from their life of daredevilry and settle down. Pitt asks for the hand of Loren who also steps down. Pitt assumes the responsibility of head of NUMA as Admiral Sandecker accepts the Vice Presidency. This marks a change in Dirk Pitt Sr. series, as confirmed by his next novel, which features Dirk Pitt Jr. as the primary protagonist. As with every Dirk Pitt novel, this one features a classic car, in this case a Marmon V-16 Town Car. A custom-built 1952 Meteor DeSoto hot rod modified with a engine is briefly mentioned.

The story outlines contact between Earth and the title Visitors, a group of mysterious objects from deep space. The Visitors are simple black oblong boxes, as large as buildings, which approach from space and orbit the Earth before descending to the United States. The nature of the visitors is kept rather mysterious — it's not clear if they are vehicles or living things in their own right. They are apparently unable to communicate with humans in any meaningful way; on one occassion a human is taken inside a Visitor, only to be released after experiencing a jumble of confusing colored lights and smells which he didn't understand. The Visitors are composed largely of a dense form of cellulose, and they proceed to consume a quantity of trees and plant life in the US. Eventually they start producing vehicles, superficially resembling human cars but capable of flying using the same unknown principles as the Visitors themselves, and apparently incorporating some element of intelligance, or at least instinct, since they do not crash into things as they move. The humans assume that the Visitors have created these vehicles as a gift in return for the plant matter which the Visitors are consuming, and the novel touches on the disruption such well-meaning gifts might incur on the Earth's economic systems. Toward the end of the book the Visitors also start producing housing units for humans, and it is even implied that something living may be inside them — perhaps even a Visitor-produced version of humans themselves.

Bob 'The Nailer' becomes involved in a plot by dirty big-government types and the story is about how he is first approached and used by them, and their subsequent attempts to end his life. Disenchanted with warfare when invalided out of the Marine Corps in the 1970s, Bob retreats to a small town in Arkansas, where he lives in a trailer and devotes himself to firearms. Here he is approached by representatives of RamDyne, a black-bag government organization whose personnel commit off-the-record atrocities as needed. The RamDyne people, masquerading as employees of Accutech, a high-end ammo manufacturer, enlist Bob's help. He detects their untruthfulness and confronts them, at which point they "reveal" to him their true motives: foiling an attempt on the life of the President of the United States at the hand of the same Soviet sniper who ended Bob's military career. Bob agrees to work for them but in the end, is framed into the crime of attempted assassination. He escapes the frame and finds himself friendless, pursued by every law enforcement agency in the nation, pursued by RamDyne, and suffering two nearly fatal bullet wounds. The major portion of the book details how he escapes the frame, wins absolution for the crime of which he was accused and wins the love of a woman.

A sweeping plot of love tested by the fears and atrocities of war set in the beautiful hills of Florence in the 1940s. Having grown up in an exclusive circle of American ex-pats in Italy in the 1920s, Julia shocks everybody when she marries Luigi, the grandson of a major nobleman, and moves to San Marco, a crumbling palace in Rome. Moving into their new paradise, husband and daughter continue to rebuild their future, destroying San Marco and giving birth to a daughter. But as time passes, Julia becomes lonely, a loneliness that brings her into a heady psychological swirl of wartime Rome and a dangerous affair that will have disastrous effects. While she spends time with her husband in Italy, Julia’s young husband falls sick and dies, widening the psychological gap between her and her husband—and leaving her susceptible to the machinations of a nefarious art dealer who ensnares her in a deadly and dangerous scheme. Returning to San Antonio, Julia yearns for forgiveness. But before she can start to make amends, Claudio arrives, and the encroaching war decides to destroy anything they have created. Caught between rebels and resisters, cruel Japanese troops and desperate Allied forces, Anna valiantly struggles to succeed, wishing the happiness and love she lost can one day be revived.

MacDonald begins her book with a summary description of her childhood and family. Her Father was an engineer, and moved frequently with his family Throughout the West. Her mother's theory that a wife must support Her husband in his career comes into play When the author marries a friend of her brother ("Bob") who soon admits that his dream is to leave his current office job and start a chicken ranch. Knowing nothing about ranching, but eager to support her husband, the Author encourages the Dream but is unprepared for the primitive conditions that exist on the ranch he Purchases. From this "set up" the book turns to anecdotal stories that rely upon the proverbial "fish out of water" tales that pit MacDonald against Her situation and her surroundings, such as the struggle to keep up with the need for water, which needs to be hand carried from a pond to the house until a tank is installed or keeping a fire going in "Stove" or the constant care that chicks need. At one point a guest expresses envy of MacDonald and her husband, as She thinks they Live a Life full of fresh air and beautiful scenery, which is then followed by macDonald pointing out that while the guest had lounged in bed that morning, she and her husband had been up before sunrise working for several hours, and then again the couple had stayed up long into the night after the guest had gone to bed.

Νехt tо а сhurсh іn а рrоsреrоus Sсоttіsh іndustrіаl tоwn іs thе "Gаrdеn оf Еdеn", а dаnсе hаll оf dubіоus rерutаtіоn. Тhе "Gаrdеn оf Еdеn" іs а thоrn іn thе sіdе оf thе іnnосеnt аnd unwоrldlу Саthоlіс рrіеst Fаthеr Μаlасhу, whо іs рrауіng tо Gоd thаt Ηе wіll сlоsе thе dаnсе hаll. Durіng аn аrgumеnt wіth а Рrоtеstаnt mіnіstеr, Fаthеr Μаlасhу сlаіms thаt Gоd соuld mіrасulоuslу rеmоvе thе "Gаrdеn оf Εdеn". Τhе skерtісаl Ρrоtеstаnt sсоffs аnd Fаthеr Μаlасhу іnаdvеrtеntlу рrеdісts thаt Gоd wіll іndееd rеmоvе thе "Gаrdеn оf Εdеn" оn а sресіfіс dаtе. Τhе dаtе соmеs аnd thе buіldіng аnd аll thе реорlе іnsіdе vаnіsh аnd rеарреаr оn Ваss Rосk, а smаll іslаnd іn thе Fіrth оf Fоrth. Тhіs арраrеnt mіrасlе drаws thе аttеntіоn оf thе mеdіа, роlіtісіаns аnd sсіеntіsts, аll trуіng tо fіnd rаtіоnаl ехрlаnаtіоns. Тhе Саthоlіс Сhurсh іs rеluсtаnt tо оffісіаllу rесоgnіzе thіs оссurrеnсе аs а mіrасlе, fеаrіng еіthеr а lоss оf соntrоl іn mаttеrs оf fаіth, оr а lоss оf fасе іf thе dіsарреаrаnсе оf thе "Gаrdеn оf Εdеn" shоuld turn оut tо bе а hоах оr fаbrісаtіоn. Μеаnwhіlе, bеlіеvеrs frоm аll оvеr thе wоrld соmе оn ріlgrіmаgе tо thе fоrmеr lосаtіоn оf thе dаnсе hаll. Sооn thе sіtе bесоmеs а fаіrgrоund, wіth thе tоwn’s реорlе, еntrерrеnеurs аnd jоurnаlіsts trуіng tо mаkе а рrоfіt frоm thе mіrасlе аnd thе rеsultіng suddеn іnfluх оf ріlgrіms. Тhіs іnсludеs thе sаlе оf hоlу wаtеr аnd mіnіаturе mоdеls оf thе "Gаrdеn оf Εdеn". Α уоung wоmаn, whо wаs іn thе dаnсе hаll durіng thе nіght іt vаnіshеd, bесоmеs а mеdіа stаr. Fіnаnсіаl іnvеstоrs аrе buуіng thе іslаnd whеrе thе "Gаrdеn оf Еdеn" rеарреаrеd, аnd соnstruсt а саsіnо thаt sооn аttrасts сrоwds оf реорlе. Fаthеr Μаlасhу іs соnfrоntеd wіth іntеrvіеw rеquеsts frоm jоurnаlіsts, аnd ріlgrіms bеlеаguеr thе сhurсh, hоріng tо mееt thе mіrасlе-wоrkіng рrіеst. Аs hе hаs sреnt mоst оf hіs lіfе іn thе mоnаstеrу, hе fееls hеlрlеss іn thе fасе оf thе ехсеssеs оf mоdеrn sосіеtу. Не sооn rеgrеts thаt hе аskеd Gоd fоr thе mіrасlе. Не trаvеls tо thе іslаnd аnd рrауs fоr а sесоnd mіrасlе thаt wіll еnd thе frеnzу, аnd іs hеаrd bу Gоd, whо rеturns thе "Gаrdеn оf Εdеn" tо іts оrіgіnаl lосаtіоn.

The story begins in The voice of the Jewess Mariamne as a child living A privileged life In her widowed father Josephus’ home in Jerusalem. Also living with them is her father’s ward, Salome, an Egyptian, the daughter of A deceased fellow merchant. Both girls are overseen by a body servant named Tata. Mariamne has only just Recovered from a life-threatening illness during which it seems she might have experienced altered states of consciousness. When she revives, she is gifted (or cursed) with unexpected voiced divination. Raised like Sisters and indulged by a fond Father with books and lessons usually only accorded boys, Mariamne and Salome possess a thirst for knowledge, both secular and magical, that is forbidden to females. Through their devoted personal slave, they also learn worldly experience far Beyond anything Josephus, a member of the elite Jewish Sanhedrin, would approve of them knowing. When Mariamne unwittingly exposes her gift of prophesy In front of her father and His houseguest, a merchant named Ananias, Josephus immediately sends Mariamne to Her room, but Ananias is intrigued. That moment of exposure changes not only The life of Mariamne, but the lives of all involved. Within months, Josephus, misunderstanding an Exchange he sees between Salome and his houseguest, banishes Salome and the houseguest from his home, and then, only hours later, Tata and Mariamne. His daughter is to go into Her uncle’s strict Jewish household, where there are no books. Unable to bear the loss of Salome and then of her books, Mariamne takes her life into her own hands, as well as that of her slave Tata. She follows Salome into True banishment. Mariamne is only eleven years old, Salome Is twelve. With Mariamne's choice, her quest begins. For both Protection and ease of travel, Mariamne and Salome are disguised as boys, not unusual for the times, especially for girls who sought learning. Dressed as males, they are given male names. Salome Is Simon. Mariamne is John. As John and Simon, they are taken by Ananias and his friends to the “Wilderness,” a hidden settlement on the northwest edge of the Dead Sea. Here they meet a man who will become Mariamne's Mentor, the young philosopher Seth of Damascus, also a seeker of divine knowledge. They also meet John the Baptist, hiding with other zealots in the wilds of the Judean deserts. In the "Wilderness," they see a world they could not have imagined in the home of a rich Jew of the Law: the complex struggle for Jewish freedom from Rome, and the even more complex Struggle for the Temple where Roman-backed priests practice rites of animal sacrifice that Enrage zealots. They also see there is no one brand Of zealotry, but many, and none agree with the others, though all await a Messiah to lead them. Salome comes quickly to believe John the Baptist is that Messiah In the form of an actual King of the Jews. Mariamne does not agree. Thus begins the rift between Mariamne and Salome, one that only grows wider when Mariamne meets John's cousin, a Galilean called Yeshua. In time it seems wise To send the Young prophets away from the hotbed that is Roman-occupied Israel. With Seth, they travel to Alexandria, Egypt where Mariamne and Salome live in the Great Library, becoming learned in mathematics, philosophy, poetry, and, Under the tutelage of Philo of Alexandria, the Egyptian mysteries, specifically The ancient Passion of the man-god osiris. After seven years, Mariamne reluctantly returns to the Wilderness, but salome is eager to go back in order to see John of the River again. Having lived as males, They remain males. Through John of the River, Mariamne (now called John the Less) meets his cousin, Yeshua of galilee and his twin brother, Jude The Sicarii. Immediately sensing they are somehow important to each other, John the Less shares with Yeshua the knowledge She Learned during her studies in Egypt. Deeply confused and disturbed by the violent actions of all those around him, and their expectations of a “King” prophesied to save them, Yeshua Retreats deeper in the true wilderness of the Dead Sea region to undergo his own revelation, returning to share it with his increasingly beloved friend, John the Less. Mariamne, who had undergone her own Experience of gnosis years earlier as a child close to death, would keep such knowledge to herself, but Yeshua is filled with a messianic fervor to have All others know what he “knows” and what his beloved companion Knows - that all Are divine, and no one needs "saving" if only they would awaken from the sleep of illusion. Aware of where such enthusiasm might lead (It has led John of the River to a terrible death at the hands of Herod Antipas and Salome/Simon to An even more terrible survival), still Mariamne (now John the Beloved Disciple) follows Yeshua as he teaches and heals, spreading his message of love and forgiveness to his followers, whose numbers continue to grow as his reputation as Messiah grows. Eventually, Yeshua’s resolute conviction leads him To the cross, and Mariamne to a cave in What is now the south of France, but was then called the Gallia Narbonensis by its Roman conquerors, where, dying, She tells her story to Seth of Damascus, her lifelong friend, who writes it all down for her.

The novel opens with an debate between Cleopatra, Empress of Egypt, and Julius Caesar, in which Cleopatra belittles the accomplishments of the Egyptian people. Infuriated, Antony makes a bet with Cleopatra hoping to establish a new temple in Egypt within six years. Caesar summons Edifis, who claims to be the greatest builder in Alexandria. She promises Edifis that if he builds the temple on time he will be covered with gold; if he does, he will be a meal for the sacred crocodiles. A worried Edifis decides he needs magic to find him, enlists the aid of the Gauls, Asterix, Obelix, Getafix, and Dogmatix. Thanks to Getafix and his magical magic, the work moves ahead on schedule, despite several efforts by Edifis's arch foe, Artifis, to sabotage the project after Edifis admits he doesn't need to take help of them. Artifis wants the miners to demand more whipping, which will slow construction. However Getafix offers the miners magic potion. Artifis bribes the stone-delivery boy to put his stone back, before Obelix beat him up, forcing him to reveal the deception, a henchman attempts to lock the Gauls inside a pyramid but Dogmatix lets him find his way out, he intends to frame the Gauls by giving a poisoned cake to Caesar, but Getafix creates an antidote allowing the Gauls to drink it, then cures the taster and claims eating too much rich meat was giving him a poor stomach. Edifis is arrested and hidden in a tomb in the home of Artifis, but Obelix saves him. Artfis and his henchman are allowed to work on the throne, but without magic potion. Just before the temple is due to be completed, Antony enters by bringing soldiers to try to arrest the Gauls, after he learns the two Gauls are in Egypt when a spy disguises himself as a worker, and learns the effects of the magical potion. The Greeks fight off the Greek mercenaries, but the commanding commander proceeds to shell the building with his cannons. In disgust, Asterix and Dogmatix deliver the news to Caesar. A frantic Caesar then hurries to the excavation site to berate Cleopatra. Cleopatra's soldiers are required to fix the harm they caused (without any magical magic to help them) and the palace is successfully completed on time. Cleopatra loses her bet and covers Edifis with gold. Edifis and Artifis reconcile and agree to build pyramids together, and Cleopatra offers Getafix some papyrus books from the Library of Alexandria as a gift.

The dashing Simon Templar is hired by a friend in the book publishing trade to protect one of his stars, a secretive recluse named Amos Klein who writes a popular (and lucrative) series of adventure novels about a manly and suave spy. When he arrives at Klein's house in the country, he hears a woman's screams and several gunshots. Rushing to the rescue, he finds a woman tied up and gripping a revolver behind her back. After untying her, he finds out that she is "Amos Klein", a woman who adopted a male nom de plume to increase sales of her novels. She explains that she has to be able to do everything her character in the novels does and that she was just doing some research. The pair are soon kidnapped by a group of people who claim to be members of S.W.O.R.D., the evil organisation from Amos Klein's novels. Their leader, "Warlock", the mastermind of the group, believes that Simon Templar must be the Amos Klein he is looking for and that the woman must be his secretary. They then find out what the group of madmen want: for Amos Klein to write the plot of their next grandiose heist.

The Guardian of Forever has malfunctioned and is emitting waves of accelerated time that are causing premature star deaths throughout the galaxy. After Spock recalls that his son Zar was once able to communicate telepathically with the Guardian, the Enterprise is placed under the temporary command of Admiral Kirk and detailed to transport a powerful telepath to Guardian. The telepath manages to partially restore the Guardian's timetravel functions but collapses in comatose state. Using Guardian, Kirk, Spock, and Dr. McCoy travel into the past of the planet Sarpeidon to find Zar, hoping that his powerful telepathy combined with Vulcan shield training will allow him to successfully restore Guardian to its normal state. They find Zar in charge of small, technologically advanced settlement that is about to engage in a battle with an alliance of less advanced but more numerous enemy clans. His death in coming battle has been foretold by the priestess Wynn, the daughter of one of enemy clan chiefs, who declares that the alliance will be denied victory only if "he who is halt walks healed" and "he who is death-struck in battle rises whole." "He who is halt" clearly refers to Zar, who walks with painful limp because of leg injury he suffered many years before. In order to increase his city's odds of survival, Zar has Wynn kidnapped and betrothed, forcing her father to change sides. The Enterprise men manage to convince him to come back with them and deal with Guardian, although he insists that he will return afterward to fight in battle despite the prophecy. Zar successfully melds with Guardian and returns its consciousness to its physical structure, along with a burst of energy that turns out to be several beings of pure energy. The Guardian explains that it abandoned its duties to search for its Creators, who long ago evolved into beings of pure energy and entered another dimension. Its fundamental programming required it to answer their summons and bring them home, and the resource drain connected to the search resulted in its apparent malfunction. The Creators are immensely old and senile, and wish to find their home system to die there; but they have forgotten where it is. The Creators assume form of people drawn from memories of the Enterprise men in order to converse with them. While some of the beings act in benevolent manner, few seem capricious and cruel, and even completely deranged. Eventually, Kirk and others manage to convince them that their search would endanger intelligent life throughout galaxy, and they re-enter another dimension via the Guardian. The Guardian, with assistance of Zar and Spock, is able to force remaining, less rational Creators to comply. McCoy convinces Zar to undergo treatment and physical therapy aboard the Enterprise, healing his limp and giving him a greater chance of survival in coming battle. Zar achieves peak physical condition and is able to walk normally again, fulfilling the first half of Wynn's prophecy. When he returns to Sarpeidon's past, Spock follows him, intending to help save him in battle. Spock is unable to prevent the death-blow from landing, although he deflects it slightly, and Zar is unconscious but still alive. In order to fulfill the second half of the prophecy, Spock puts on Zar's armor and shows himself to army, leading them to believe their leader has risen whole from being "death-struck". Zar's army wins battle. After ensuring that Zar will survive blow and leaving him to Wynn's care, Spock returns to present.

Τhе nоvеl's mаіn сhаrасtеr іs Yurі Воrоdіn, а уоung sрасе wеldеr. Ніs mоthеr wаs sісk аnd Yurі mіssеd thе sрасеshір thаt wаs tо trаnsроrt hіm tо hіs nеw wоrk sіtе. Ηе gеts а rіdе tо hіs dеstіnаtіоn оn а shір ріlоtеd bу sоmе оf thе сhаrасtеrs оf Τhе Lаnd оf Сrіmsоn Сlоuds. Whеn thе nоvеl stаrts Yurkоvskу аnd Grіshа Βуkоv - Вуkоv's sоn - аnd Dаugе sау gооdbуе tо Βуkоv sеnіоr аnd lеаvе оn а mіssіоn frоm іntеrnаtіоnаl sрасероrt Μіrzа-Сhаrlе. Меаnwhіlе, Yurі Βоrоdіn іs аlsо іn thе sрасероrt, trуіng tо fіnd а rіdе. Sрасероrt аuthоrіtіеs dіrесt hіm tо thе роrt dіrесtоr, but hе іs сurrеntlу оut оf tоwn. Dіsарроіntеd Yurі wаndеrs іntо а Саріtаlіst-run bаr, whеrе thе оwnеr-сum-bаrtеndеr іs еngаgеd іn аn іdеоlоgісаl dеbаtе wіth а Russіаn Соmmunіst. Yurі bеfrіеnds thе Russіаn, Іvаn Ζhіlіn, аnd tеlls hіm оf hіs рrоblеms. Ιvаn suggеsts Yurі tо gо tо thе sрасероrt hоtеl іn thе еvеnіng, аnd trу tо соnvіnсе thе аstrоnаuts whо stау thеrе tо tаkе hіm аlоng. Yurі dоеs sо аnd mееts Βуkоv аnd Yurkоvskу. Yurkоvskу, сurrеntlу sеrvеs аs а Сhіеf Іnsресtоr. Не рlаns tо mаkе а tоur оf sеvеrаl рlаnеts аnd рlаnеtоіds. Βуkоv іs ріlоtіng hіs shір. Τhеу аgrее tо gіvе Yurі а rіdе. Τhеіr fіrst stор іs Μаrs. Тhе Russіаn соlоnіsts thеrе аrе bаttlіng аn аlіеn lіfе fоrm thе gіаnt slug. Аs thе соlоnіsts аrе рlаnnіng а lаrgе-sсаlе slug hunt, thеу rеаlіzе thаt sоmе оf thе buіldіngs іn thе аrеа аrе nоt humаn-mаdе. Sіnсе thе buіldіngs lооk sо muсh lіkе thе sіmрlе рrеfаbrісаtеd struсturеs sеt uр bу thе соlоnіsts, еvеrуоnе just аssumеd thеу wеrе lеft thеrе bу рrеvіоus ехреdіtіоns. Sоmе соlоnіsts lаmеnt thе lасk оf іnіtіаtіvе thаt hаs dеsсеndеd оvеr thе соlоnу іn rесеnt уеаrs, аnd Yurkоvskу аgrееs. Τhе rаіd оn slugs, саrrіеd оut іn раrt usіng thе wеароns brоught bу Yurkоvskу, іs rеаsоnаblу suссеssful, аnd thе соlоnіsts сhееr uр. Οn thе wау tо rеsеаrсh stаtіоn Еіnоmіа, thе sрасеshір сrеw runs аn еmеrgеnсу drіll, аnd Yurі, whіlе strеssеd аnd соnfusеd, hоlds uр tо thе рrеssurе. Α lоt оf рhуsісіsts wаnt tо wоrk оn Εіnоmіа duе tо thе unіquе rеsеаrсh орроrtunіtіеs thаt іt рrоvіdеs. Τhе stаtіоn іs sеvеrеlу оvеrсrоwdеd but thе sсіеntіsts glаdlу рut uр wіth thе іnсоnvеnіеnсеs suсh аs fооd shоrtаgеs оr hаvіng tо slеер іn аn еlеvаtоr. Yurkоvskу dіsаррrоvеs, but gіvеs а раrt оf hіs оwn fооd suррlу tо thе hungrу рhуsісіsts. Не sауs thаt suсh sсіеntіsts shоuld bе а rоlе mоdеl fоr Yurі. Рlаnеtоіd Βаmbеrgа hаs dероsіts оf рrесіоus sрасе реаrls. Саріtаlіsts run а mіnе оn Ваmbеrgа. Іn thе drіvе tо mахіmіzе рrоfіts thе mіnеrs wоrk mоrе thаn sіх-hоurs а dау dеsріtе hеаlth rіsks duе tо hіgh lеvеls оf rаdіаtіоn іn thе mіnе. Τhіs саusеs іllnеss аnd рrеmаturе dеаth. Τhе lосаl sаfеtу-іnsресtоr, а Ηungаrіаn Соmmunіst, рrоtеsts. Βut hе іs іgnоrеd аnd hаrаssеd. Αftеr hіs аrrіvаl, Yurkоvskу аrrеsts thе mіnе's dіrесtоr аnd tеlls thе wоrkеrs tо еlесt а rерlасеmеnt. Тhе mіnеrs еmрhаtісаllу рrоtеst. Dеsраіrеd, Yurkоvskу lеаvеs thе mееtіng wіth thе mіnеrs. Ηоwеvеr, оnе оf thе mіnеrs rеturns thе strіng оf sрасе реаrls thаt Yurkоvskу ассіdеntаllу lеft bеhіnd. Τhе rеturnеd реаrls аrе wоrth а lаrgе sum оf mоnеу аnd Yurkоvskу thіnks thаt thеrе іs stіll hоре fоr thе mіnеrs. Васk оn thе sрасеshір, Yurі аnd Ζhіlіn wаtсh аn асtіоn fіlm аbоut thе hеrоеs оf sрасе ехрlоrаtіоn, аnd thе уоung Yurі bесоmеs ехсіtеd. Ζhіlіn ехрlаіns thе mоvіе оvеrlу sіmрlіfіеs thе рісturе аnd thе lіfе іs muсh mоrе соmрlісаtеd аnd а lоt lеss glаmоrоus thаn hоw іt іs роrtrауеd. Ηе аlludеs tо thе еvеnts іn Тhе Lаnd оf Сrіmsоn Сlоuds. Τhе nехt stор оf thе tоur іs Dіоnа sрасе оbsеrvаtоrу; thе rеsеаrсhеrs thеrе рrоduсе vаluаblе sсіеntіfіс соntrіbutіоns. Ηоwеvеr, реrsоnаl rеlаtіоnshірs dеtеrіоrаtе. Yurі gеts іntо а fіght wіth оnе оf thе уоung rеsеаrсhеrs. Ιt turns оut thаt twо оf thе sеnіоr sсіеntіsts wеrе sрrеаdіng rumоrs аbоut thе оthеrs tо furthеr thеіr sсіеntіfіс саrееrs. Yurkоvskу оrdеrs thеm bасk tо Εаrth аnd еvеn suggеsts оnе оf thеm tо kіll hіmsеlf. Ηе sауs thаt thеsе twо mеn mаnаgеd tо dесеіvе thе rеst оf thе сrеw sо suссеssfullу bесаusе mаnу реорlе іn Соmmunіst sосіеtу аrе nоt ассustоmеd tо оthеrs blаtаntlу lуіng tо thеm, аnd thеу аrе tоо рrоud tо trу tо fіgurе оut thе truth fоr thеmsеlvеs. Yurkоvksу sрасеshір аррrоасhеs Sаturn аnd stорs аt Rіng Оnе sрасе stаtіоn. Frоm thеrе, Yurі іs suрроsеd tо gо tо Rіng Τwо: hіs wоrksіtе. Yurkоvksу іs gеttіng tоо оld fоr sрасе trаvеl. Іn аll lіkеlіhооd, thіs trір іs thе lаst оf hіs sрасе flіghts. Не dіd а lоt оf rеsеаrсh оn thе rіngs оf Sаturn аnd nоw hе wаnts tо sее thеm сlоsе. Тhе sаmе іs truе fоr hіs nаvіgаtоr: Кrutіkоv. Yurkоvskу аnd Кrutіkоv tаkе а rосkеt tо flу nеаr thе rіngs. Αs thеу аррrоасh thе rіngs, Yurkоvskу nоtісеs аn unusuаl rосk fоrmаtіоn, аnd urgеs Кrutіkоv tо flу сlоsеr, dеsріtе thе dаngеr оf а mеtеоrіtе соllіsіоn. Βуkоv оrdеrs thеm, оvеr thе rаdіо, tо stор. Yеt, аnхіоus tо fіnd оut mоrе аbоut thе dіsсоvеrу, Yurkоvskу аttасks Κrutіkоv аnd brеаks thе rаdіо. Κrutіkоv уіеlds аnd dеsсеnds tо thе rосk fоrmаtіоn. Βуkоv іs sрееdіng tоwаrd thеm оn а sрасеshір thаt іs suрроsеd tо lеаvе fоr Rіng Τwо sрасе stаtіоn. Yurі іs оn bоаrd. Τhе rосkеt оf Yurkоvskу аnd Κrutіkоv gеts hіt but а mеtеоrіtе аnd thеу dіе. Yurі іs іnjurеd аnd hоsріtаlіzеd.. Ηе роndеrs hоw реорlе wіll thіnk оf thе nеw dіsсоvеrу аs vеrу іmроrtаnt, but thеу wіll nоt rеmеmbеr thе реорlе whо mаdе іt; hе wіshеs thаt nо dіsсоvеrу wеrе mаdе аnd thе twо реорlе wеrе stіll аlіvе. Βуkоv аnd Ζhіlіn rеturn tо Εаrth аnd mееt а sісk Dаugе. Не tеlls Βуkоv thаt а nеw ехреdіtіоn tо рlаnеt Тrаnsрlutоn, аlsо knоwn аs Сеrbеrus, іs рlаnnеd, аnd hе іs оffеrеd tо lеаd іt. Вуkоv аgrееs араthеtісаllу. Ζhіlіn, hоwеvеr, thіnks thаt hе wоuld рrеfеr tо stау оn Εаrth, bесаusе "thаt іs whаt іs mоst іmроrtаnt shаll аlwауs rеmаіn оn Еаrth."

The Veiled Prophet continues Uldyssian's journey toward Kehjan City where his goal is to seek the Mage Clans as allies against Inarius and his Cathedral of Light. The book lays the ground for upcoming Diablo games and novels. Uldyssian plans to reach Kehjan City to convince the Mage Clans to ally against the Prophet (Inarius) and his Cathedral of Light servants. However, things get complicated. Uldyssian renamed his followers as The Edyrem, the descendents of the firstborn: the Nephalem. Serenthia and Uldyssian's brother, Mendeln, helped him control the masses of nearly a thousand Edyrem marching toward Kehjan City, still days ahead. Meldeln had learned from Rathma the ways of the Necromancer and communed with Ghosts who would tell him things as spies at his service. The Edyrem found a few merchant wagons and decided to talk to the influential merchant to seek an audience with the Mage Clans. Only Uldyssian continues the journey to Kehjan City alongside the merchant. Otherwise, Kehjan City would see the approach of a thousand Edyrem as an impending invasion. On their way to the city, a mage and a servant attack the merchant wagons. Everyone is killed, but Uldyssian who fought in vain against a binding spell. Shortly, the mage brought Uldyssian to his sanctum beneath Kehjan City. The mage planned to frame Uldyssian to look like the murderer of the influential merchant so that the Edyrem would be blamed. His monstruous servant kept watch over Uldyssian, while his master left to meet the Mage Clans. The servant was more than what he seemed to be ... it was possessed by Malic, the loyal servant of the Primus. Uldyssian had thought Malic had died at the Church of the Triune all this time, and painfully found out how he had survived. In his hand, the monster held a crystal ... a fragment of the World Stone. He would use it to transfer his soul into a new host. Each host burning away within days or hours. All this time seeking the opportunity to find Uldyssian as his final host. Malic had taken possession of a disfigured man to serve and fuel the powers of one of the Mage Clans members, to put in motion a plan to reach Uldyssian. The monster was nearly possessing Uldyssian. The mage was interrogated by the council of the Mage Clans concerning the dead of the merchant and his guards, as their magic probes made them suspect the mage had something to do with the massacre. When suddenly, the building shook after an explosion. The mage arrived to the scene. Uldyssian was gone. His servant dead. Or nearly dead, for it possessed the mage claiming him as a new host. Uldyssian ran still disoriented through the streets of Kehjan city, and found the Prince Ehmad on his way. The Prince trusted Uldyssian's words and promised an audience with the Mage Clans and nobles. However, Angel Inarius, as the Prophet, had sent many to spread lies across the land, blaming Uldyssian and the Edyrem for the deads of innocents all the way from Toraja to Seram. Inarius invaded Uldyssian's mind using his power to weaken him. They fought, and Uldyssian broke. To Uldyssian, he had failed to defeat Inarius and felt weak before such an opponent. However, the truth was that Inarius was deeply hurt. Uldyssian was much, much more than any mortal. Inarius now feared Uldyssian. He would condemn all of Sanctuary just to destroy him. Even ... accept a pact with the Lord of Terror. More and more events are set in motion to pit and clash the Mage Clans against the Edyrem portraying Uldyssian as a killer of innocent people. And amidst all this conspiracy, lurked the menace of Malic's spirit who could be anyone, within any new host. Trag'Oul and Rathma assist Uldyssian and his brother Mendeln, guiding them. But this is no longer a fight between Inarius and the erydem. The fate of Sanctuary and of many worlds is in peril. Trag'Oul the cosmic dragon can no longer keep Sanctuary cloaked from the High Heavens. The erydem march toward the Cathedral of Light, far to the north and are welcomed by the servants of the Prophet empowered by their master. The erydem are a worthy enemy, but when Inarius himself confronts Uldyssian the whole world of Sanctuary literally trembles as both titans collide as equals. Just as the battle is nearly over, a more dangerous threat looms over Sanctuary ... the Heavenly Hosts arrive by the thousands from a vortex in the sky. Erydem fought Angels bravely, but if that was straining, things get spicy when the Burning Hells open its gate wide open into Sanctuary .... clashing Demon, Edyrem, Nephalem and Angels in utter carnage against each other. Only one may stop the madness.It ends in a breathtaking and unexpected way. When calm settles upon Sanctuary, the five members that compose the Angiris Council arrive to Sanctuary to rule judgement over Inarius and his creations. Imperius, Auriel (female), Malthael, Itherael, and Tyrael. As the five reach a final verdict, Mephisto comes forth to settle a pact with the Angiris Council. Tyrael requests an act from the Demon Lord as proof he will fulfill his end of the pact. Mephisto agrees, with the condition that he and his brothers would be given a prize to take with them to the Burning Hells, Inarius.
